chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib Al-Ghalib Al-Asadi, from his father, from Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab, who said:

I was present with Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) one day when he prayed the morning prayer, and behold, a beggar was at the door. So Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'Give to the beggar and do not repel a beggar.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali (AS) say about repelling beggars?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith highlights the practical piety of Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn (AS), who prioritized the dignity of the supplicant even during the performance of morning prayer. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *sabr* (patience) and *karam* (generosity) as active virtues, reinforcing the principle that repelling a beggar is a spiritual loss. The narration serves as a foundational text for the etiquette of charity, linking immediate material aid with spiritual purification.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyar, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Ghalib Al Asady, from his father, from Saeed Bin Al Musayyab who said,

‘I was present with Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> one day when he<sup>asws</sup> Prayed the morning Prayer, and there came a beggar at the door. So Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Give to the beggar and do not repel a beggar’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ghalib al-Asadiy from his father from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyib who has said the following: “

I visited Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, one day after he had performed the Morning Prayer. At that time, someone asking for help appeared at the door and Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘Give something as charity to one who asks for help and do not turn away such people empty- handed.’”
